standard_prerequisites.name: Induction principle of the circle
standard_prerequisites.statement: For P : S^1 -> U with b : P(base) and a dependent path over loop from b to b there is f : prd x:S^1 P(x) with f(base) := b and apd f (loop) equal to the given path.
standard_prerequisites.use: The whole proof is one application of this principle to the constant family lam x. A at source lines 290-291, and its output at lines 295-299 is stated with apd, not ap.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in a constant family
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a constant type family the transport along any path is the canonical identification transconst A p a : trans A p a = a.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the datum p : a = a into the dependent path required by the induction principle at source lines 292-294, and it is the term that has to be cancelled at source line 303.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dependent paths
standard_prerequisites.statement: dpath B p u v unfolds to trans B p u = v, so a dependent path over loop from a to a is a path between transports of a.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof works throughout with the type dpath (x |-> A) loop a a and its relation to a = a, at source lines 291-294.

core_obligations: Apply the induction principle of S^1 to the constant family (lam x. A) rather than to an arbitrary family, noting that the required hypothesis at base is exactly the given point a : A (source lines 290-291).
Produce the second hypothesis as a dependent path in dpath (x |-> A) loop a a; this is not the datum p : a = a itself but the composite transconst A loop a `ct` p (source lines 292-294).
Read off the resulting f : S^1 -> A with f(base) := a and apd f (loop) = transconst A loop a `ct` p, i.e. the dependent computation rule (source lines 295-299).

Derive the non-dependent rule ap f (loop) = p: use the identity apd f (loop) = transconst A loop (f base) `ct` ap f (loop), combine it with the previous line and cancel the two transport terms, which are identical because f(base) is definitionally a (source lines 300-303).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the recursion principle to the circle induction principle applied to the constant family, using transconst to turn p : a = a into the required dependent path.
Apply the principle to obtain f with its base and dependent loop computation rules.
Recover the non-dependent computation rule by the constancy of apd and cancellation of equal transport terms.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.2.5 at source lines 279-288: for a type A with a : A and p : a = a there is f : S^1 -> A with f(base) := a and ap f (loop) := p. The author's proof (source lines 289-304) is not the one-line appeal to the induction principle that the lead-in promises: applying the circle induction principle to the constant family at lines 290-291 demands a dependent path in dpath (x |-> A) loop a a, which is not p but its composite with transconst A loop a (lines 292-294), so the principle at lines 295-299 only yields the dependent rule apd f (loop) = transconst A loop a `ct` p. Recovering the non-dependent rule needs the separate identity at lines 301-302 and a cancellation that closes only because f(base) is definitionally a (line 303).
